spec.target: customer defaults within the next 90 days
spec.prediction_time: scored on the 1st of each month using data available to the prior month end
spec.preprocessing: numeric features standardised within training folds only

features.name: months_on_book
features.description: account tenure in months at scoring

features.name: recovery_amount
features.description: dollars recovered by collections after the account was charged off for this default

features.name: collections_calls
features.description: number of collections calls placed about this default episode

label.rationale: Recoveries and collections activity only exist *because* the customer defaulted; both are recorded after the outcome and are unavailable at scoring time. They are direct consequences of the label.

spec.target: patient is readmitted within 30 days of discharge
spec.prediction_time: scored at the moment of discharge
spec.split: random 80/20 split stratified by the label
spec.preprocessing: one-hot encoding fit on the training split

features.name: primary_diagnosis
features.description: ICD code for the index admission

features.name: readmit_drg
features.description: DRG billing code of the readmission encounter

label.rationale: readmit_drg is the billing code of the readmission itself; it can only be populated once a readmission has occurred, so it encodes the label.

spec.prediction_time: scored in real time at authorisation
spec.preprocessing: amount log-transformed; encoders fit on train only

features.name: chargeback_filed
features.description: whether the cardholder later filed a chargeback disputing this transaction

label.rationale: A chargeback is filed days to weeks after the transaction and is a downstream consequence of fraud; it is not known at authorisation.

spec.prediction_time: scored monthly on the active subscriber base
spec.split: split by calendar month (train earlier months, test later)

features.name: support_tickets_90d
features.description: tickets opened in the last 90 days

features.name: cancellation_reason
features.description: reason code the retention agent records when a subscriber calls to cancel

label.rationale: cancellation_reason is captured only during a cancellation call, so it exists only for churners and directly reveals the outcome.

spec.target: units sold of a SKU in the upcoming week
spec.prediction_time: forecast produced on the Friday before the target week
spec.preprocessing: lag features; scaling fit on train only

features.name: promo_flag
features.description: whether a promotion actually ran during the target week; the promo calendar is finalised at month end, after the forecast

label.rationale: promo_flag describes the target week itself and is only finalised after the forecast is made; using it injects future information.

spec.preprocessing: bureau features standardised on train only

features.name: bureau_score
features.description: credit-bureau score pulled at the quarterly portfolio review, six months after origination

label.rationale: The bureau score is a snapshot taken six months after the prediction point; at origination that future value is unknown.

spec.target: length of stay for an admitted patient
spec.prediction_time: predicted at the hour of admission
spec.preprocessing: imputation fit within each training fold

features.name: num_procedures
features.description: total number of procedures performed during the entire stay

label.rationale: The procedure count accrues across the whole stay and is only final at discharge; at admission it lies in the future.

spec.prediction_time: scored at the instant the impression is served
spec.preprocessing: hashing encoder fit on train only

features.name: user_ctr_7d
features.description: user click-through rate over prior 7 days

features.name: dwell_time_s
features.description: seconds the user spent on the landing page during this session

label.rationale: Landing-page dwell time happens only after a click and after the impression decision; it is unavailable at impression time.

spec.preprocessing: StandardScaler fit on the entire dataset before the train/test split, then the same scaler applied to both parts

label.rationale: Fitting the scaler on all rows before splitting leaks test-set statistics (mean/variance) into training.

spec.prediction_time: scored when the claim is filed
spec.preprocessing: missing values imputed with the column mean computed over all rows (train and test together) before folds are created

label.rationale: Global-mean imputation computed over all rows lets each fold's validation data influence the imputed values used in training.

spec.preprocessing: SMOTE oversampling applied to the full dataset to balance classes, then the balanced data is split into train and test

label.rationale: Oversampling before the split copies/synthesises minority points that then appear (or inform neighbours) in both train and test.

spec.preprocessing: the top 200 TF-IDF terms are selected by mutual information with the label computed on all rows, then cross-validation is run on the reduced feature set

label.rationale: Supervised feature selection using the label over all rows (including test) is a classic leak; selection must happen inside each fold.

spec.notes: Each patient contributes several studies over time.

label.rationale: Patients have multiple images; a random per-image split puts different images of the same patient in both train and test, inflating scores. The split should be grouped by patient_id.

spec.preprocessing: text vectoriser fit on train only
spec.notes: A minority of reviewers account for most reviews.

label.rationale: Prolific reviewers write many reviews in a recognisable style; random splitting leaks a reviewer's style across train and test. Split by reviewer_id.

spec.notes: Thousands of hourly rows per machine.

label.rationale: Consecutive hourly rows from one machine are highly correlated; a random split leaks a machine's regime across train and test. Use a machine-grouped (or time-based) split.
Repeat applicants submit multiple applications with near-identical attributes; random splitting leaks the same applicant across folds. Group by applicant_id.

features.name: record_id
features.description: auto-increment row id; confirmed-fraud accounts were bulk-loaded into the table last, so larger ids skew fraudulent

label.rationale: record_id is an artefact of load order that correlates with the label; it carries no causal signal and must be dropped.

features.name: mrn
features.description: medical record number; a specialist cancer centre with a high malignancy rate was assigned a contiguous MRN block

label.rationale: The MRN range encodes the site, and site is correlated with the outcome; the model can exploit the id instead of clinical signal.

spec.split: the first 80% of rows are used for training and the last 20% for test
spec.preprocessing: no shuffling is applied before the split

features.name: row_index
features.description: position of the row in the delivered file

label.rationale: The file is sorted with all spam first; an unshuffled positional split makes row_index (and the split itself) a proxy for the label.

features.name: source_file
features.description: which vendor file the row came from; vendor A supplied only converted leads and vendor B only non-converters

label.rationale: source_file perfectly separates the classes by construction of the merge; it is a label proxy, not a usable feature.

spec.target: customer defaults within the next 90 days
spec.prediction_time: scored at month end using only prior data
spec.split: time-based split, train earlier than test
spec.preprocessing: standardisation fit within each training fold only

features.name: utilization_ratio
features.description: balance over limit at month end

features.name: last_payment_date
features.description: date of the last payment made before the scoring date

label.rationale: All features are known at scoring time; last_payment_date is a past event and the scaler is fit per fold. No leakage.

spec.split: split by customer so no customer appears in both train and test

features.name: avg_monthly_usage_gb
features.description: mean data use over prior 3 months

label.rationale: Features are all pre-scoring and the split is grouped by customer, avoiding group leakage.

spec.prediction_time: forecast on the Friday before the target week

features.name: planned_promo_flag
features.description: whether a promotion was *scheduled and locked* before the forecast date for the target week

label.rationale: The promo flag here is the plan locked before the forecast date, so it is legitimately known at prediction time (contrast with TE01).

spec.preprocessing: log transform; encoders fit on train only

features.name: account_age_days
features.description: days since the account was opened

label.rationale: Every feature is available at authorisation time; account_age_days is a past-dated duration, not future information.

features.name: discharge_disposition
features.description: where the patient was discharged to (home, SNF, ...)

label.rationale: discharge_disposition is decided at discharge (the prediction time) and the split is patient-grouped. No leak.

spec.target: annual claim cost for a policy
spec.prediction_time: scored when a quote is produced

label.rationale: All inputs are declared at quote time; policies are independent so a random split is fine.

spec.split: split grouped by machine and ordered in time

label.rationale: Features use only information up to the prediction hour and the split is grouped by machine; no group or temporal leak.

features.name: campaign_id
features.description: random UUID assigned to each send, independent of the outcome

label.rationale: campaign_id is a random identifier uncorrelated with the label; the RFM features are pre-send. The id mention is a benign distractor.
Property attributes are all known at listing; the date is used only to form the split, not as a feature.

spec.preprocessing: hashing encoder fit on train only

label.rationale: All features are available when the impression is served; nothing uses post-click information.

spec.target: employee leaves within 6 months of the review
spec.prediction_time: scored on the annual review date

label.rationale: The review-date snapshot precedes the 6-month outcome window; all features are known at review time.

features.name: items_in_cart
features.description: items in cart at the decision point

features.name: is_returning_user
features.description: whether the user has purchased before

label.rationale: Features are measured up to the add-to-cart decision and the split is user-grouped; nothing uses the post-decision session tail.

spec.target: patient develops sepsis in the next 6 hours
spec.prediction_time: scored each hour using vitals up to that hour

label.rationale: Only information available up to the scoring hour is used, and the split is patient-grouped and time-ordered.

spec.prediction_time: scored before the offer is sent

label.rationale: All inputs are pre-offer; the outcome (acceptance) occurs after scoring. No leakage.

spec.target: hours to resolve a support ticket

label.rationale: Fields are all set at ticket creation; tickets are independent so a random split is appropriate.

spec.target: electricity demand for the next hour
spec.prediction_time: forecast at the top of the current hour

features.name: temp_forecast_next_hour
features.description: weather-service temperature forecast for the next hour, issued before the prediction time

label.rationale: A forecasted temperature issued before prediction time is legitimately available; it is a published forecast, not realised future data.
